title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
Under the Roads for Development Program (R4D), the Government of Timor-Leste (GoTL) has rehabilitated 55.25 km of core rural roads in 2020. Works tendered under the 2019 General State Budget and implemented during 2020 generated US $ 15.04 million in contracts for 66 Timorese-owned contractors during the year, 19 (30%) of which were women-led firms. During 2020 R4D works employed 5,286 short-term workers (234,798 worker-days) of which 944 (18%) were women and 33 (0.6%) were persons with disability - created an estimated 1,021 jobs (full-time equivalent). System of GoTL to manage rural road is now strengthened, with the finalization of the Integrated Roads Management System (IRMIS). During 2020, road inventory and condition assessment form for site data collection was finalized. The Government is also now used advanced procurement system, which has also been approved and operational with the commencement of procurement of 2021 contracts, in 2020. The Rural Road Master Plan and Investment Strategy (RRMPIS) also continued to be the guiding document for planning, budgeting and implementation of rural roads. Capacities of relevant R4D GoTL agencies' staff continues to improve in relation to technical skills, including GIS, engineering skills, procurement and contracts supervision.
The following results were achieved by GoTL through the Partnership for Sustainable Agro-Forestry (PSAF): During 2020-2021, through the capacity building and labour-based programme for Contractors, rural roads have been rehabilitated and maintained to improve access and market linkages to agro-forestry communities, including 64.8 km of rural roads leading to agro forestry area in Baucau, Viqueque, Manatuto and Lautem, and 36.4 km of roads maintained thus providing improved market access. 4,317 workers were employed, realizing 204,362 worker days. Women participation is at 23.4%, and 2% of people with disabilities. 34 Local civil works contractors trained. With funding from the Government of Australia, the ILO has supported the GoTL to implement the Roads for Development Program (R4D), executed by the National Directorate of Roads, Bridges and Flood Control (DRBFC) of the Ministry of Public Works (MPW). This included: (1) Provision of technical assistance to R4D in implementing local resource-based approaches to rural roadworks that are community-based and emphasise social inclusion and gender equality. (2) Development of the Integrated Roads Management System (IRMIS), for centralizing planning, budgeting, procurement, traffic management, contracts management and progress monitoring data. (3) Support annual update and implementation of the Rural Road Master Plan and Investment Strategy (RRMPIS). (4) Conducted 42 training events, totalling 2,095 trainee-days for 281 (51 women) relevant DRBFC staff. (5) Producing guidelines and manuals for rural roads, including COVID-19 occupational safety and health response guidelines for the safe return of contractors and workers to R4D rehabilitation and maintenance sites; (6) Continue promoting gender equality, women's empowerment, and disability inclusion by promoting participation in in rural road activities.
With funding from the European Union (Enhancing Rural Access Agro-Forestry), the ILO provided: (1) Technical support for implementing rural roads rehabilitation and maintenance programme by adopting employment intensive investment approaches to improve access and market linkages to agroforestry areas, and enable employment creation and economic opportunities; (2) Advisory and technical support in the institutional capacity building of DRBFC, Don Bosco Training Centre and Institution for Business Development Support and Staff from Baucau, Manatuto, Viqueque and Lautem municipalities; (3) Integration of social safeguards including gender, disability inclusiveness, safety, health in the implementation of rural road rehabilitation.
